questions.question: What is a training dataset? What is its purpose in Machine Learning?
questions.solution_html:
• A training dataset is a collection of data used to train a Machine Learning model by helping
  • it learn patterns and relationships in the data. - (1 mark). Purpose: It enables the model to
  • learn from examples and make predictions or decisions on new, unseen data. – (1 mark)
  • True Positive (TP): The model correctly predicts the positive class. 2. True Negative (TN)
  • Page 1 of 6
  • The model correctly predicts the negative class. 3. False Positive (FP): The model
  • incorrectly predicts the positive class when the actual class is negative. 4. False Negative
  • (FN): The model incorrectly predicts the negative class when the actual class is positive.
  • Example - Consider a Machine Learning model that predicts whether students will pass or
  • fail an examination. – (2 marks)
  • Actual Predicted Pass (Positive) Fail (Negative)
  • Pass (Positive) TP = 40 FN = 10
  • Fail (Negative) FP = 5 TN = 45
  • Interpretation
  • - TP = 40: 40 students who actually passed were correctly predicted as passed.
  • - TN = 45: 45 students who actually failed were correctly predicted as failed.
  • - FP = 5: 5 students who actually failed were incorrectly predicted as passed.
  • - FN = 10: 10 students who actually passed were incorrectly predicted as failed.
  • Forward propagation: Input data passes through the network to produce a predicted
  • output.
  • Calculate the gradients of the loss function. 2. Update the weights and biases using an
  • optimization algorithm. 3. Repeat the process until the loss is minimized or a stopping
  • condition is reached. Example: Gradient Descent is a commonly used optimization
  • algorithm. – (3 marks)
  • Initialize i to n.
  • Data Privacy and Security - Machine Learning systems often use large amounts of
  • personal data. Developers must protect sensitive information and obtain appropriate
  • consent before collecting and using data. Proper security measures should be
  • implemented to prevent unauthorized access and data misuse. Example: A healthcare
  • prediction system must protect patients' medical records and personal information. – 2
  • marks
  • Collect the Data
  • Supervised Learning - Supervised Learning is a type of Machine Learning in which
  • a model learns from labelled data containing both input features and their
  • corresponding outputs. Working: - The model is trained using labelled data. - It learns
  • the relationship between inputs and outputs. Classification and regression belong to
  • supervised learning. It predicts the output for new, unseen data. Example: Predicting
  • house prices using previous housing data containing house areas, numbers of rooms
  • and actual prices. Applications: Email spam detection, house price prediction, and
  • disease diagnosis. – (4 marks)
  • Steps Involved in Constructing a Decision Tree – (5 marks)
  • Step 1: Collect the training data
  • Step 2: Select the best splitting attribute - Choose the attribute that best separates the
  • training examples into different classes. Entropy and Information Gain are commonly
  • used for this purpose.
  • Step 3: Create the root node - Select the best splitting attribute as the root node of the
  • tree.
  • Step 4: Divide the dataset - Split the dataset into subsets according to the possible
  • values of the selected attribute.
  • Step 5: Repeat the process - For each subset, select the next best attribute and repeat
  • the splitting process until the stopping condition is reached.
  • Step 6: Create leaf nodes - Create a leaf node when all examples in a subset belong
  • to the same class or when another stopping condition is satisfied.
  • Step 7: Prune the tree- Remove unnecessary branches that may cause overfitting and
  • reduce the model's ability to generalize to unseen data.
  • Overfitting: A very deep tree may learn noise and unnecessary details from the
  • training data. 2. Instability: Small changes in the training data can produce a
  • significantly different tree. 4. Greedy approach: The algorithm selects the best split at
  • each step, but this does not guarantee a globally optimal tree. 5. Complexity: Large
  • trees can become difficult to interpret.

  • Overfitting - A decision tree may learn the training data too well, including noise and outliers.

questions.solution_html:

  • while removing irrelevant or redundant features. It helps improve the performance of a Machine
  • Learning model. – (1 mark)

questions.question: Demonstrate the working principle of BIRCH and mention its advantages.
questions.solution_html:
• Demonstrate the working principle of BIRCH and mention its advantages.
  • BIRCH stands for Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering using Hierarchies. It is
  • appropriate for very large datasets or for streaming data, because of its ability to find a
  • good clustering solution with only a single scan of the data. Instead of storing all data
  • points, BIRCH stores compact summaries called Clustering Features (CF). A CF
  • contains the following. Number of data points (N), Linear sum of points (LS) and
  • Squared sum of points (SS). – (4 marks). Advantages - Fast and memory efficient.
  • Suitable for very large datasets. Handles incremental data insertion. Reduces
